# Urbo CMS Backend

> **Start here:** `just up` from the repository root brings the whole stack up for the worktree
> you are in — this backend included, in a container, with the database seeded. You only need the
> manual steps below when you are working *on* the backend and want a Gradle restart loop, which
> is what `just backend-local` sets up for you. See
> [`scripts/urbo/services.mjs`](../scripts/urbo/services.mjs)'s header comment for how instances
> are isolated.
>
> Ports and hostnames in the sections below are the pre-instance defaults. Under `just up` every
> URL carries the instance label — `http://api.<instance>.localhost` — and only Postgres is
> published on the host, on a port `just up` prints.

Welcome to the Urbo CMS Backend! This guide will help you get started with setting up and running the application.

## Requirements

Before you begin, please ensure you have the following installed:

* [Docker](https://www.docker.com/products/docker-desktop)
* [JDK 25](https://jdk.java.net/25/) (required only if you are not using Docker to run the Spring application.)

## Setting Up

Prerequisites: You need a personal access token to Github, either as environment variable `GITHUB_TOKEN` or as gradle
property `swcodeGprKey`. The access token is required to build the project, because it needs to pull packages from
Github.

1. Get a personal access token key on [your Github settings](https://github.com/settings/tokens).
2. Enter your secret token in as `GITHUB_TOKEN` environment variable.
   Alternatively, place your `swcodeGprKey=ghp_xxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxx`
   in your `%USERPROFILE%\.gradle\gradle.properties` along with your username,
   but this does not work with the docker workflow.
3. Remember to restart your terminals and all containers.

All local services are exposed via an nginx reverse proxy using `*.localhost` subdomains — under
`just up`, one per instance. No `/etc/hosts` changes are needed for browsing: `.localhost` is the
reserved TLD browsers resolve straight to `127.0.0.1` with no DNS lookup at all, and — unlike a name
that merely resolves to loopback — it also gets the frontends a secure context, which Keycloak's
login flow needs (see `scripts/urbo/services.mjs`'s `publicHostname`).

Which *other* tools resolve these names varies by platform and by tool; on Windows the system
resolver does not, so `ping` and the like fail on them. See
[the root README](../README.md#development) for the details.

| Service | URL |
|---------|-----|
| Backend API | http://api.\<instance>.localhost |
| Keycloak | http://keycloak.\<instance>.localhost |
| MeiliSearch | http://meilisearch.\<instance>.localhost |
| Mailpit | http://mailpit.\<instance>.localhost |
| Sendinblue Mock | http://sendinblue.\<instance>.localhost |
| LocalStack (S3) | http://localstack.\<instance>.localhost |
| imgproxy | http://imgproxy.\<instance>.localhost |
| LimeSurvey | http://limesurvey.\<instance>.localhost (opt-in, see [LimeSurvey](#limesurvey)) |
| PostgreSQL | localhost, on the port `just up` prints each run — `just status` shows it again (Postgres is the only service published on the host; everything else is reached through the proxy, above) |

`just urls` prints the rest of this list already filled in for your instance.

We have two workflows to launch the backend:

- Test workflow: Uses docker so you don't have to install JDKs to build the backend once.
- Dev workflow: Uses your local Java setup with your installed versions, built for hot reloading.

### Tester workflow

The former `spring/docker-compose.spring.yml` overlay is gone: the backend container (`spring-app`,
built from the multi-stage `Dockerfile` — no local JDK required) is now part of the main Compose
file and is started by `just up` from the repository root, image build included. The one-shot
`sample-data-loader` container it also starts waits for the backend `/health` endpoint and then
seeds demo data in three phases (push-integration content, curated categories, admin resources) —
see [Docker Sample Data](#docker-sample-data) for the full layout.

On an instance that was seeded before, `just up` asks whether to re-seed; `--seed` and `--no-seed`
answer that up front:

```bash
just up --no-seed
```

To rerun only the sample data import after changing files in `docker/sample-data/`, from the
repository root, against an already-`up` instance:

```bash
docker compose --env-file .urbo/<instance>/env -f backend/docker/docker-compose.yml \
  --profile seed up sample-data-loader
```

### Dev workflow

`just backend-local` (see the banner at the top of this file) is the fast Gradle restart loop: it
runs `./gradlew :urbo-app:bootRun` on the host, wired to the environment `just up` already
rendered for this instance — the same Postgres, Keycloak, MeiliSearch, etc. the containerised
backend uses, with Postgres reached through its published host port. Run it against an
already-`up` instance, after stopping the containerised `spring-app` first (both would otherwise
fight over the same database and Keycloak realm) — `just backend-local` prints the exact command
for that, or run it yourself:

```bash
docker compose --env-file .urbo/<instance>/env -f backend/docker/docker-compose.yml stop spring-app
